summary.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of ~260m (30% margin) included ~46m of one-offs; adjusted ~304m (35%), with gases segment margin 40% in Q4 and 38.4% for FY26.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA was about 260 million at a roughly 30% margin, but management cited three non-recurring items totalling about 46 million (leave-encashment provision 11m, impairment on a legacy non-core investment, and a 15m settlement with an on-site customer over plant start-up date), taking adjusted EBITDA to about 304 million (about 35%). Core gases segment revenue grew 9% QoQ in Q4, and FY26 core gases revenue grew 14.2% over FY25, with reported growth held back by the delayed start of Uluberia 2. Argon prices recovered from Q3 lows but remain below 1H FY26 levels. Management framed FY27 as an execution year with a stronger capacity base, but gave no numeric guidance beyond a 20% revenue CAGR target over the next 2-3 years.

Gases segment EBITDA margin, Q4 FY26 (adjusted for one-offs)

financial_highlights.value: 8% to 10% (per analyst's reading of YoY split)

segments.name: Core gases (merchant, packaged, on-site)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue growth 14.2% over FY25; gases segment EBITDA margin 38.4% for FY26 and about 40% in Q4 after adjusting one-offs. Existing plants ran at high utilisation, with Uluberia 2 the exception as a recent commissioning.

segments.name: Argon (by-product of oxygen)
segments.commentary: Argon prices were weak in Q3 FY26 on soft steel demand and oversupply from captive plants, and recovered in Q4 but remain below 1H FY26. Management targets argon at about 15% of revenue over the longer term, versus 8-10% currently.

segments.name: Project engineering (EPC for external clients)
segments.commentary: Management does not expect significant growth; the in-house team is fully engaged on internal expansion projects and bills only for external projects.

guidance_outlook: No specific quarterly or annual numeric guidance for FY27; management said the direction is positive and revenue contribution from new capacity will be more meaningful.
Medium-term revenue CAGR target of about 20%, to be achieved over the next 2-3 years.
Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 40% in the medium term, driven by efficient new capacity, lower power cost via renewables and PPAs, argon recovery and operating leverage.
Merchant capacity to rise from about 900 TPD to about 1,130 TPD within 12 months; on-site from about 700 TPD to about 1,000 TPD.
Merchant capacity to reach about 1,350 TPD by FY28 after two further merchant plants (about 450-500 TPD combined) in northern and west-central India.
FY26 capex target of about 250 crore; management expects to deploy the full amount over FY27 run-rate through the year (phrased as full-year FY26 target in Q&A).
capex_capacity: Uluberia 2 merchant plant (220 TPD, West Bengal) commissioned in Q4 FY26; in ramp-up with an assumed 18-month ramp, with revenue expected to rise every quarter for 6-8 quarters.
East India on-site plant of 320 TPD expected to be commissioned in the next month (around June 2026); on-site contracts are take-or-pay fixed-amount arrangements.
Another 220 TPD merchant plant expected to be commissioned within FY27; a further ~250 TPD merchant plant early in FY28 (northern and west-central India).
Specialty gases debulking facility planned within the west-central India plant to serve solar cell manufacturers.
Current merchant capacity ~900 TPD (southern region ~550 TPD); on-site ~700 TPD. Ability to execute plants above 1,000 TPD cited.
demand_pricing: Argon prices recovered in Q4 from Q3 lows but remain below 1H FY26; management expects further recovery, supported by steel-sector demand and solar, and says argon is structurally tight since supply is tied to oxygen capacity.
Management says long-term contracts govern pricing, and it does not foresee a price war from new ASU capacity.
Existing non-Uluberia capacity is fully utilised; growth depends on new capacity additions.
Power is the largest cost line; transport is second. Typical delivery radius is 300-400 km. Grid tariff is about 50-60% higher than the PPA tariff; exchange power is slightly below grid.
Renewable PPA covers about 170 TPD (about 18% of ~900 TPD merchant capacity) via a wind-solar hybrid; PPA covers 55-60% of one factory's power demand. Targets PPAs for all three southern plants.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q4 one-offs and are they recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Three items totalling about 46m: 11m employee leave-encashment provision, impairment on a legacy non-core investment, and a 15m settlement with an on-site customer over plant start-up date. Management said these are non-recurring and the 15-year customer contract continues.

qa_highlights.question: Will project engineering revenue grow significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant growth expected; the team is fully engaged on internal projects, which generate no billing, and external projects are unlikely to fit with planned capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for argon prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 prices recovered from Q3 but are below 1H FY26; management urged viewing argon on an annual average basis and expects it to remain robust with steel-sector demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% CAGR achievable and how do capacity additions translate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% revenue CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with no single-year guidance, supported by the Uluberia 2 and East India on-site plants and further merchant additions.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA margin and power cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term aspiration is 40% EBITDA margin, supported by efficient new plants, renewable and PPA power, argon recovery and operating leverage. Management said power cost will decline as a percentage of revenue but not to about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Renewable share of power and PPA plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% of merchant capacity is on a renewable PPA; the target is PPAs for all three southern plants, subject to state policy and customer-premises constraints.

risks_watch: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin (about 35%) is well below the 38% level seen in 1H FY26, and FY26 margins depend on argon recovery continuing.
Execution risk on Uluberia 2 ramp-up (18-month assumed) and on the East India on-site plant commissioning expected around June 2026.
Reported growth was held back by delayed commissioning; the 20% CAGR target depends on new merchant and on-site capacity coming on stream on schedule.
Possible further one-offs or disputes on on-site contract start-up dates, given the 15m settlement this quarter.
Competition from new ASU capacity across the industry; management disputes the price-war risk but offered no quantified pricing outlook.
Capex commitment of about 250 crore for the year; the company said it has not stated how much has been spent to date.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structural demand and the 20% CAGR and 40% margin targets, but cautious on near-term argon pricing and avoided specific FY27 numbers. Management was evasive on the quarterly argon outlook and on the unit economics detail, referring analysts elsewhere.
